# DRAFT-015: Complete the Android pipeline — `pipeline-android.env`, `run_analysis-android.sh`, and a shared `clone.pl`

**Status:** **[#28](https://github.com/evilbootloader/drakvuf-multios-sandbox/issues/28) — published and closed 2026-08-19.** Drafted, not published — 2026-08-15
**Area:** android / core
**Milestone:** M3 (Android MVP)
**Priority:** P1
**Depends on:** DRAFT-033 (hard — the template's error handling, and the
`VG_NAME`/`CLONE_LV_SIZE` environment reads this issue consumes),
DRAFT-028b (hard — creates `platform.env`, which C4 requires this issue *not*
duplicate). DRAFT-009/#6 supplies C1–C10. DRAFT-013/#13 and DRAFT-037/#7 are
landed and supply the evidence.
**Blocks:** DRAFT-016 (hard, on all three deliverables).
**Origin:** `docs/checklists/android.md` §2.3, §2.4, §2.5.

> **Retitled on drafting.** The index row reads "Implement `clone-android.pl`
> per checklist §2.5". Two things are wrong with that as a scope statement.
>
> **It is too narrow.** C1 required five files per OS pipeline. DRAFT-016
> owns two of them and explicitly assigns the other three here
> (`DRAFT-016.md:391`, `:611`), and `docs/checklists/android.md:798` already
> assigns `pipeline-android.env` here by name. Left as written, this issue
> delivers one file and DRAFT-016 stays blocked on two more that no issue
> owns. (The third of those three is the clone script, which the decision
> below turns from a new file into a rename — but it is still this issue's.)
>
> **And §2.5 is not the specification.** Of its eighteen required changes,
> **one is already done**, **ten belong to DRAFT-033**, one is owned by
> nobody, and two are answered by evidence rather than by code. The
> disposition table below goes through all eighteen.

> **Decided 2026-08-15: there is no `clone-android.pl`. The clone step
> becomes shared `automation/clone.pl`.**
>
> The finding behind it: `clone-ubuntu.pl` contains, today, exactly **one**
> value that is Ubuntu-specific — `-L64G` (`clone-ubuntu.pl:280`).
> Everything else is passed in on the 3-argument contract, derived from
> those arguments, or host-global. Once that one value comes from the
> environment as `CLONE_LV_SIZE`, the per-OS content of the file is **empty**,
> and a `clone-android.pl` written per C1 would be a byte-identical copy —
> the duplicate-and-drift failure C2 exists to prevent, arriving through a
> file C1 happens to classify per-OS.
>
> **This amends C1**, which is a decided outcome of issue #6. C1 becomes
> "four per-OS files plus the shared clone script"; C2's list of shared files
> grows from four to five. Recorded here, and in
> `docs/architecture/analysis-pipeline.md`, as an amendment rather than an
> exception — the next OS pipeline must read the amended rule, not discover
> this issue.
>
> The maintainer took this decision on 2026-08-15 together with the
> `CLONE_LV_SIZE`-from-environment half; it is not the draft's to take.

# Objective

Complete the Android pipeline so that an Android sample can be cloned, and so
DRAFT-016 has a configuration file and a launcher to be written against.

Three deliverables:

1. `automation/pipeline-android.env` — new, per C3/C4.
2. `automation/run_analysis-android.sh` — new, per §2.4.
3. `automation/clone-ubuntu.pl` → `automation/clone.pl` — renamed and made
   shared, with `CLONE_LV_SIZE` read from the environment.

Under C1 as amended that is four per-OS files for Android
(`pipeline-android.env`, `preconfig-android.sh`, `drakvuf-android.sh`,
`run_analysis-android.sh`) plus a shared clone script — two of the four
belonging to DRAFT-016.

# What DRAFT-013 already settled — this script automates a transcript

The clone script is not speculative work. The entire sequence was executed
by hand on Dom0 on 2026-08-14, against the current template, and recorded in
`docs/runbooks/verify-android-isolation.md` steps 2–3. The script's job is to
produce that transcript from three arguments.

```bash
# verify-android-isolation.md:238 — the snapshot
sudo lvcreate -s -n android_sandbox-13-clone -L32G /dev/vg-root/android_sandbox

# :243-249 — the three config rewrites, by hand
name = "android_isolation_test"
disk = [ 'phy:/dev/vg-root/android_sandbox-13-clone,hda,w' ]
vif  = [ 'type=ioemu,model=e1000,script=vif-openvswitch,bridge=xenbr1.1' ]

# :288 — the restore
sudo xl restore -p -e /root/android_isolation_test.cfg \
    /root/sandbox_project/state/android_sandbox.bak
```

Compare that against what `clone-ubuntu.pl` generates when it is handed
`android_sandbox`, `1`, `misc/android_sandbox.cfg`:

| Hand-written on 2026-08-14 | Generated by the existing script | Match |
|---|---|---|
| `name = "android_isolation_test"` | `name = "android_sandbox-1-clone"` | equivalent — see below |
| `disk = [ 'phy:/dev/vg-root/android_sandbox-13-clone,hda,w' ]` | `disk = [ 'phy:/dev/vg-root/android_sandbox-1-clone,hda,w' ]` (`:237`) | **exact shape** |
| `vif = [ '…,script=vif-openvswitch,bridge=xenbr1.1' ]` | strips `bridge=`/`script=`/`backend=`, keeps `type=ioemu,model=e1000`, appends both (`:220-231`) | **exact** |
| `xl restore -p -e <cfg> …/state/android_sandbox.bak` | `…/state/$origin.bak` via `FindBin::RealBin` (`:283,291`) | **exact** |
| `lvcreate -s … -L32G` | `-L64G` (`:280`) | **the one difference** |

Two things follow, and they are the substance of this issue.

**The `name =` rewrite is not merely equivalent, it is safer.** The runbook
carries a warning at `:253-258`: on 2026-08-12 the config said
`android_sandbox_test` while the operator drove `android_isolation_test`, and
`xl network-list` returned `invalid domain identifier (rc=-6)` before anyone
noticed. The script derives the domain name and the config's `name =` from
the same `$clone` variable, so that class of slip cannot occur. The runbook
says the same: *"harmless there, but the same slip in an automated path is a
clone that never gets checked."*

**The `hda` question §2.5 raises is answered by evidence, not by code.**
`misc/android_sandbox.cfg:59` and `misc/ubuntu_sandbox.cfg:54` are the same
line but for the LV name, and the manual clone above restored, unpaused, ran
for 99 seconds and passed eleven isolation steps on `hda`. §2.5's *"do not
blindly assume `hda` without verifying the restored VM expects it"* is
discharged by citation. It is worth keeping the underlying caution for
DRAFT-034 — see "Out of scope".

# What this issue owns

## 1. The clone script becomes shared

Line by line, here is every value in `clone-ubuntu.pl` that is not passed in
on the 3-argument contract. This table is the whole argument for the rename:

| Value | Line | Class | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$lvm_vg = "vg-root"` | `:142` | host-global (C4) | DRAFT-033 → `$ENV{VG_NAME}` |
| `$clone_bridge = "xenbr1"` | `:145` | host-global (C4) | DRAFT-033 → `$ENV{ANALYSIS_BRIDGE}` |
| `$vif_script = "script=vif-openvswitch"` | `:152` | host-global (C4) | DRAFT-033 |
| `hda` in the disk rewrite | `:237` | per-OS *by nature*, identical in practice | evidence above |
| `-L64G` | `:280` | **per-OS (C3)** | DRAFT-033 → `CLONE_LV_SIZE` |
| `state/$origin.bak` | `:283` | derived from argv | already correct |

`analysis-pipeline.md` is explicit that the size is the per-OS one: *"the
clone LV size is not among them — it is per-OS … Windows will want more,
Android likely less. `CLONE_LV_SIZE` belongs in `pipeline-<os>.env`, with
`64G` as Ubuntu's default."* Android's value is **32G**, and it is measured,
not guessed: `android_sandbox` is a 32,00g LV
(`verify-android-isolation.md:975`) against `ubuntu_sandbox`'s 64,00g, and
32G is what the manual clone used.

Once DRAFT-033 moves the first three rows to the environment and the fifth to
`CLONE_LV_SIZE`, **nothing OS-specific is left in the file.** The 3-argument
contract already carries origin, VLAN and config — every OS-varying input —
and the environment carries the rest. So the file is renamed
`automation/clone.pl` and shared by all three pipelines.

`run_analysis-<os>.sh` points `dirwatch`'s clone-script argument at the shared
path. That is a per-OS decision made in a per-OS file, so **nothing becomes
OS-aware**, which is the test `analysis-pipeline.md` already applies to the
config split: *"a shared script reading a host-global config does not make it
OS-aware — that is the test."* The same holds for a shared script reading a
per-OS one.

**What this amends.** C1 becomes four per-OS files plus the shared clone
script; C2's shared-file list grows from four (`dirwatch.c`,
`network-setup.sh`, `cleanup.sh`, `tcpdump.sh`) to five. Both edits land in
`analysis-pipeline.md` in this issue's change, not as a note here — the point
of C1–C10 is that a reviewer can check them without reading the issues that
produced them.

**What it costs.** One rename of a deployed path, which DEPLOY handles below;
and C1's "exactly five files, and no others" stops being a pure count. Set
against a second and eventually third copy of a file with no per-OS content,
which is what the development rule *"prefer parameterization over duplicated
hard-coded values"* forbids and what C2 exists to prevent everywhere else.

**How the size reaches the Perl.** By the mechanism decision 3 of
`analysis-pipeline.md` already specifies for the host-global values — no new
one, and no config parser in Perl:

```perl
# in clone.pl, replacing the literal at :280
our $clone_lv_size = $ENV{CLONE_LV_SIZE} // '64G';
```

`run_analysis-<os>.sh` sources `pipeline-<os>.env` and exports it;
`dirwatch` spawns every callback with `envp = NULL`
(`dirwatch.c:178,190,216,380,400`), which inherits the parent environment.
The defaults the file carries today become the fallbacks, so an unset
variable reproduces current behaviour exactly.

> **That inheritance is source-reasoned, not execution-evidenced** —
> `analysis-pipeline.md` flags it as GLib's documented behaviour for
> `envp = NULL`, unconfirmed on Dom0. It matters more for the size than for
> the others: a silently empty `$ENV{VG_NAME}` falls back to `vg-root` and is
> almost certainly right, but a silently empty `$ENV{CLONE_LV_SIZE}` falls
> back to `64G` and **an Android clone still works** — it just allocates
> twice the exception store it needs, against a VG that also holds two 64G
> Ubuntu volumes and a 256G root. The failure is invisible at the clone and
> shows up later as VG pressure. The TEST section checks the size explicitly
> rather than inferring it from a successful clone.

> **Ordering: DRAFT-033 lands first, on `clone-ubuntu.pl`, unrenamed.** It is
> already committed to the environment reads (`analysis-pipeline.md:526-533`
> assigns the wiring there) and to parameterizing the snapshot size
> (`DRAFT-033.md:249`); this issue then does the `git mv` and updates the
> callers. Renaming first would only mean DRAFT-033 opens a file under a name
> the rest of the backlog does not yet use, for no gain.
>
> DRAFT-033's title — *"…before it is copied twice"* — is left alone. Its
> premise no longer holds, but every fix in it is still required: the file is
> now shared by three pipelines instead of copied into three, which raises
> the cost of its defects rather than lowering it.

> **One shared-code observation, recorded and deliberately not acted on
> here.** `dirwatch` calls the clone script through
> `g_spawn_command_line_sync(command, &output, NULL, NULL, NULL)`
> (`dirwatch.c:178`) — the exit-status argument is `NULL`. **`dirwatch`
> cannot see a non-zero exit at all.** stdout is the only failure channel
> that exists, which is why C9's *"prints a clone domain ID to stdout **only**
> on success"* is load-bearing rather than stylistic, and why DRAFT-033's
> matching criterion (`DRAFT-033.md:244`) matters more than its exit-status
> criteria do. Changing `dirwatch` is DRAFT-010's, not this issue's.

## 2. `pipeline-android.env` — and the anchor PID is not the one the checklist records

C3 lists the required keys. Ubuntu's file supplies the shape; the Android
values below are each sourced.

| Key | Android value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `SANDBOX_DOMAIN` | `android_sandbox` | `CLAUDE.md`, "Current Android names" |
| `DOMAIN_CONFIG` | `$REPO_ROOT/misc/android_sandbox.cfg` | same rule as Ubuntu's `:55` |
| `KERNEL_PROFILE` | `$REPO_ROOT/profiles/android.json` | `CLAUDE.md`; not git-tracked |
| `SAVED_STATE` | `$STATE_DIR/android_sandbox.bak` | derived, as Ubuntu's `:72` |
| `TARGET_OS` | `android` | drives the three `/malware_*/android` paths |
| `GUEST_STAGING_DIR` | `/data/local/tmp` | execution-evidenced 2026-08-10; `pipeline-ubuntu.env:104` already names it |
| `CLONE_LV_SIZE` | `32G` | §1 above |
| `INJECTION_PID` | **`3164`** | **see below** |
| `WATCH_MODE` | `1` | as Ubuntu |
| `MAX_CLONES` | `2` | as Ubuntu — but see DRAFT-036 under "Out of scope" |
| `GUEST_NAMESERVER` | `1.1.1.1` | `pipeline-ubuntu.env:161`; divergence between copies is a defect unless written down |

**`GUEST_USER` is not in Android's file.** It is Ubuntu's mechanism for
building a staging path (`/home/$GUEST_USER/Desktop`) and Android's staging
directory is absolute. `pipeline-ubuntu.env:104` already anticipates this.
Adding an unused `GUEST_USER` to Android's copy would be C4's failure mode in
miniature — a value present because the template had it.

**The anchor PID.** `docs/checklists/android.md:798` says *"the new anchor
PID must reach `pipeline-android.env` when DRAFT-015 creates it. §1.5 is
currently the only place the value exists."* **That sentence is now false in
both halves**, and taking it at face value puts a stale PID in a new file:

- §1.5 records anchor PID **3163** against saved state `1844fc0a…`.
- The template was re-saved before DRAFT-013 ran. The current saved state is
  `516644e2…` and the current anchor PID is **3164**
  (`verify-android-isolation.md:171-172`, confirmed in that runbook's results
  matrix at `:1159`).
- `3164` appears in **exactly one file in the repository** — that runbook.
  §1.5 has not been annotated.

`pipeline-ubuntu.env:171` states the rule this instantiates: *"a long-lived
process inside the saved memory image … It is a property of the `.bak` file,
not of this config — re-saving the template almost certainly changes it."* It
did, by one.

> This is roadmap risk #12 landing for the second time in nine days. §1.5's
> own annotation says *"nothing forces this record to keep up with the
> artifact it describes"* — and then the record went stale again, in the same
> field, before anyone consumed it. Writing `3164` into
> `pipeline-android.env` does not fix that; it moves the value into a file
> that at least has one consumer. **PLAN step 3 re-reads it from the live
> template rather than trusting either document**, and DEPLOY records the
> `(checksum, PID)` pair together so a future reader can tell whether they
> still belong to each other.

## 3. `run_analysis-android.sh` — accepting DRAFT-016's proposal

`DRAFT-016.md:602-616` records that this file is owned by no draft by title,
and proposes it here on the grounds that the launcher and the config file are
one unit. **This issue accepts that**, for the additional reason §2.4 makes
plain: the launcher's job is to export `pipeline-android.env` into the
environment, and under decision 3 of `analysis-pipeline.md` that export is
also how `clone.pl` receives `VG_NAME` and `CLONE_LV_SIZE`. Splitting
the launcher from the config would split a variable from its only delivery
mechanism.

Two of §2.4's items must **not** be implemented as written:

- *"Resolve the injection anchor PID/TGID automatically / Reject zero or
  multiple matching anchors."* The anchor on this image is a backgrounded
  `nano`, chosen so the string `drakvuf` appears nowhere in the guest
  (`android.md:630-634`). §1.4's constraint is explicit: **do not build
  anchor auto-discovery on a process-name grep** — a guest running a second
  `nano` gets the wrong process injected and `injector` does not warn. Either
  key on something other than the name or keep `INJECTION_PID` a recorded
  number. **Recommendation: keep the number.** Auto-discovery that cannot use
  the name needs a criterion nobody has proposed yet; inventing one here
  would be new design inside an implementation issue.
- *"Prevent two Android launchers from running simultaneously."* Correct as a
  requirement, but it is DRAFT-033's per-launcher lock
  (`DRAFT-033.md:81-83`) and DRAFT-036's VLAN allocator. This issue must not
  grow a third locking scheme. See "Out of scope".

Ten of eighteen are DRAFT-033's, which is precisely why
`analysis-pipeline.md:515-517` orders it first: *"copy first and the defect
exists in three files."* With the clone step shared they are fixed once and
this issue inherits all of them — which is an argument for sharing that did
not exist when C1 was written.

> **The two validation items move to DRAFT-033.** With no per-OS copy, VLAN
> and name validation are changes to a shared file, and belong with the other
> sixteen rather than being applied separately here. This issue's clone-side
> work is the rename and the `CLONE_LV_SIZE` read, nothing more.

> **One §2.5 item is owned by nobody, found while writing this table.**
> *"Remove the temporary config after success or failure."* `clone-ubuntu.pl`
> writes `/tmp/$clone.config` (`:190`) and never unlinks it — on success or
> on failure. DRAFT-033 does not cover it: the file appears in that draft
> exactly once, in a table row about where `xl restore`'s stderr goes
> (`DRAFT-033.md:97`), and none of its seven CREATE items or eleven
> acceptance criteria mention it. It is not in this issue's disposition
> either, because fixing a template defect in a per-OS copy is precisely
> what the development rules forbid.
>
> Low severity — a stale `/tmp` file with no secrets in it, overwritten by
> the next clone of the same name. **Recommendation: fold it into DRAFT-033**
> as an eighth CREATE item rather than opening an issue for one `unlink`.
> Raised here because this table is the first thing to have gone through all
> eighteen items and checked each against its claimed owner.

> **DRAFT-033's line references are stale, and an executor will trip on
> them.** That draft cites the lock at `:236-241`/`:255-256`, the imports at
> `:119` and `xl restore` at `:253`. The `flock` scaffolding was removed in
> `b914123` — DRAFT-033 says so itself — so those lines have moved:
> `xl restore` is now `:291`. Re-derive line numbers when executing it; do
> not edit that draft from here.

# Dependencies

- **DRAFT-033 — hard, and it is most of the clone-side content.** Ten of
  §2.5's items, the `VG_NAME`/`CLONE_LV_SIZE` environment reads this issue
  consumes, and the stdout-only-on-success contract.
  `analysis-pipeline.md:515-517` orders it first, and that ordering survives
  the rename intact — a shared file with unchecked exit statuses is worse
  than a copied one, not better.
- **DRAFT-028b — hard.** Creates `platform.env`. C4 forbids
  `pipeline-android.env` from defining `VG_NAME`, `ANALYSIS_BRIDGE`, the
  uplink bridge or the subnet prefix, so those values need somewhere else to
  live before this file is written — otherwise the copy acquires them by
  default and C4 fails on the first grep.

  > **Assigned 2026-08-15, and it needs a "b".** `analysis-pipeline.md:526-533`
  > proposed DRAFT-028 on the grounds that it *"is already rewriting that
  > file"*, and ended *"needs confirming before it is treated as assigned."*
  > The maintainer has now confirmed it. But **DRAFT-028 deployed on
  > 2026-08-11** (`issue-index.md:577`), so the premise expired: it is not
  > rewriting anything any more, and adding scope to landed work means the
  > scope never lands. Hence a follow-on, numbered as DRAFT-028b on the
  > DRAFT-026a/b precedent, carrying `platform.env` and the
  > `network-setup.sh` wiring. `DRAFT-028.md` still says "Drafted, not
  > published" — that status is stale independently of this, and DRAFT-028b
  > should fix it while it is in there.
- **DRAFT-037/#7 — landed.** The template this clones.
- **DRAFT-013/#13 — landed.** Supplies the manual transcript, the current
  `(checksum, anchor PID)` pair, and the confirmation that a clone of this
  template survives the isolation rules.
- **DRAFT-036 — soft, and a hard gate on *running* two watchers.** Not on
  writing these files. `MAX_CLONES=2` in Android's file collides with
  Ubuntu's VLANs the moment both launchers run, because the thread-slot index
  *is* the VLAN and the slot array is process-local. Writing the file is
  safe; starting the second `dirwatch` is not.

# Out of scope

- **Any change to the clone script's error handling, locking, validation or
  diagnostics.** DRAFT-033. This issue consumes that work; it does not
  duplicate or pre-empt it. Its clone-side edits are exactly two: the rename,
  and `$ENV{CLONE_LV_SIZE}`.
- **Creating `platform.env`.** DRAFT-028b. This issue reads it and must not
  define its keys anywhere.
- **Anchor auto-discovery.** §2.4 asks for it, §1.4 forbids the only obvious
  implementation, and no alternative criterion has been proposed. Needs its
  own issue.
- **The per-launcher lock and the VLAN allocator.** DRAFT-033 and DRAFT-036.
- **Reading the disk device name from the origin config** instead of
  hard-coding `hda` (`:237`). Both current configs use `hda` so this changes
  nothing today, but it is a latent defect for DRAFT-034 — a Windows config
  using `xvda` or `sda` would have it silently rewritten to `hda`. Record it
  against DRAFT-034 rather than fixing it speculatively here.
- **`preconfig-android.sh` and `drakvuf-android.sh`.** DRAFT-016.
- **Running an Android sample.** No sample is analyzed by this issue. The
  clone is created, checked and destroyed.

# CREATE

1. `automation/pipeline-android.env` — C3 keys, C4 exclusions, `32G`, `3164`
   (or step 3's value), `/data/local/tmp`.
2. `automation/run_analysis-android.sh` — `#!/bin/bash`, as Ubuntu's launcher
   keeps (it is operator-invoked, not `dirwatch`-invoked; C8 governs the
   other four). Sources `pipeline-android.env`, pre-flights the
   `.cfg`/profile/saved state, creates `/malware_*/android`, brings the
   bridge up, runs `network-setup.sh`, exports the host-global values per
   decision 3, launches `dirwatch`.
3. `git mv automation/clone-ubuntu.pl automation/clone.pl`. No new Perl file.
   Then, in the renamed file: `$ENV{CLONE_LV_SIZE} // '64G'` in place of the
   `-L64G` literal, and a header comment saying plainly that the file is
   shared by three pipelines and carries no OS-specific value — the next
   person to add one needs to hit that sentence first.
4. Update every caller and cross-reference in the same change:
   `run_analysis-ubuntu.sh`, C1 and C2 in `analysis-pipeline.md`, the
   `automation/` file list and the known-issues list in `CLAUDE.md`, and the
   clone-script argument in both launchers.
5. Update `docs/checklists/android.md` §2.3–2.5 — the candidate blocks there
   name `/home/user/drakvuf-tools/...` paths that issue #4 removed and an
   `android-analysis.conf` that C1 renamed. §2.5's heading ("Implement
   `clone-android.pl`") no longer describes anything that will exist.

# TEST

Static, in the development container:

```sh
perl -c automation/clone.pl
bash  -n automation/run_analysis-android.sh
dash  -n automation/pipeline-android.env
shellcheck automation/run_analysis-android.sh

# C4 by grep, not by assertion:
grep -nE '^(VG_NAME|ANALYSIS_BRIDGE|UPLINK|SUBNET)' automation/pipeline-android.env
# expect: no output

# Divergence between the two pipeline files should be reviewable at a glance:
diff <(grep -oE '^[A-Z_]+=' automation/pipeline-ubuntu.env) \
     <(grep -oE '^[A-Z_]+=' automation/pipeline-android.env)
```

On Dom0 — **manual, and none of it runs in the development container:**

```bash
# Baseline first. Step 11 of the DRAFT-013 runbook compares against this.
sudo lvs -a -o lv_name,lv_size,origin vg-root
sha256sum /root/sandbox_project/state/android_sandbox.bak
sudo blockdev --getsize64 /dev/vg-root/android

# The clone test proper.
# `sudo env VAR=...`, not `sudo VAR=...` — sudo's env_reset drops the latter
# unless the variable is in env_keep, and the script would then silently use
# the 64G default. That is the failure mode described in section 1.
sudo env CLONE_LV_SIZE=32G automation/clone.pl \
    android_sandbox 1 misc/android_sandbox.cfg

# Expect on stdout: a domain ID and nothing else.
# Expect: android_sandbox-1-clone, restored PAUSED, 32G snapshot.
sudo xl list
sudo xl network-list android_sandbox-1-clone
sudo ovs-vsctl show          # the vif must carry tag: 1
# Check the SIZE, not just that a snapshot exists. A 64,00g row here means
# CLONE_LV_SIZE never reached the Perl, and the clone works anyway.
sudo lvs -a -o lv_name,lv_size,origin vg-root | grep 1-clone

# The export path itself, separately — `run_analysis-android.sh` only reaches
# clone.pl once dirwatch receives a sample, and analyzing one is out of scope
# here. So check that the launcher exports what the Perl reads:
( . automation/pipeline-android.env; echo "$CLONE_LV_SIZE" )   # expect: 32G
grep -n 'export.*CLONE_LV_SIZE' automation/run_analysis-android.sh

# Teardown, and the golden untouched.
sudo automation/cleanup.sh android_sandbox-1-clone 1
sudo lvremove /dev/vg-root/android_sandbox-1-clone
```

> **`lvremove` may report `Logical volume … in use` on the first attempt.**
> That is not a failure of this issue's code — `xl destroy` returns before
> the block device is released, and the DRAFT-013 runbook hit it at `:965`
> and succeeded on the retry (annotation at `:996`). Record which attempt
> succeeded; it is input to DRAFT-033's exit-status handling, where the same
> race causes a silent stale-snapshot reuse on the *next* sample.

Failure paths, each expecting a named diagnostic on stderr and **no clone ID
on stdout**: saved state renamed away; non-existent origin LV; malformed
VLAN; config path that does not exist.

# DEPLOY

Push, then `git -C /root/sandbox_project pull` — never while an analysis is
in flight. **The `git mv` renames a deployed file**, so confirm
`run_analysis-ubuntu.sh` resolves `clone.pl` on Dom0 before the next Ubuntu
run, and check the retired `…​.retired-issue4` checkout is not what is being
exercised.

Ubuntu is the risk here, not Android. Android has no working pipeline to
break; Ubuntu has one, and this issue renames a file in its critical path for
a reason that has nothing to do with Ubuntu. **One benign Ubuntu analysis
must complete end to end after the pull, before the change is considered
deployed** — that is the acceptance criterion, not a suggestion.

Do **not** start `run_analysis-android.sh` alongside a running
`run_analysis-ubuntu.sh` until DRAFT-036 lands. Writing the launcher is in
scope; running two watchers is not, and the collision is silent.

# Security considerations

This issue creates a clone and destroys it. No sample is staged, no sample is
executed, and nothing is written to the guest filesystem — so C6 and C7 are
not exercised. The containment posture is DRAFT-013's, already verified
against this template.

Three things are worth stating anyway, because they are properties of what
this issue *writes* rather than of what it runs:

- **The clone must land on `xenbr1.<vlan>`, never the bare bridge.** The
  DRAFT-013 runbook is emphatic: *"a guest on the bare bridge has no
  isolation rules applied to it"* (`:289-292`). The vif rewrite is the only
  thing that guarantees this, and the acceptance criterion checks the `tag:`
  rather than trusting the generated config.
- **`GUEST_NAMESERVER` is analysis-network policy, not a per-OS preference.**
  `pipeline-ubuntu.env:157` calls divergence between the copies a defect
  unless deliberate and written down. Android's file takes `1.1.1.1` because
  Ubuntu's does, not on its own reasoning.
- **A stale `INJECTION_PID` is a silent failure, not a loud one.**
  `injector` attaches to whatever PID it is given. Wrong number, wrong
  process, no warning — and on this image the anchor is a `nano` that a guest
  could plausibly run a second copy of. This is why step 3 re-reads it.

# Recovery / rollback

Two new files and one rename. Reverting is a `git revert` plus a pull on
Dom0. Nothing in this issue modifies the golden LV, the template LV, or the
saved state; the clone test operates on a copy-on-write snapshot that is
destroyed at the end. `automation/cleanup.sh` and the manual `lvremove` are
the whole teardown.

The one non-obvious rollback: Dom0 has a deployed `clone-ubuntu.pl` that the
rename removes. If the pull happens while `run_analysis-ubuntu.sh` is
running, `dirwatch` re-reads the worker scripts per sample and the next clone
fails — the Ubuntu pipeline breaks, on a change made for Android. Stop the
watcher first. This is the `CLAUDE.md` rule about never pulling in flight,
and the rename is the case where it actually bites.

# Open: one thing this issue cannot decide alone

**Does `MAX_CLONES=2` belong in Android's file at all today?**
`pipeline-ubuntu.env:182` already calls it host-global and says it is left in
the per-OS file only because DRAFT-036 will replace it outright — *"moving it
to `platform.env` first would mean moving it twice."* Copying it into a
second per-OS file makes it three moves instead of two. The alternative is
omitting it from Android's file and letting it default, which is honest about
the fact that two watchers cannot run concurrently anyway. **Recommendation:
copy it, matching Ubuntu**, so the two files stay diffable and DRAFT-036 has
one pattern to replace rather than two. Flagged rather than assumed.
